_doc: Alert code -> action. The LOCAL MODEL NEVER WRITES A COMMAND: it reads the snapshot and picks
a code, and only codes present here can execute. Everything else escalates.
Two rules are load-bearing, both learned the hard way in this pipeline:
1. NOTHING IRREVERSIBLE. No submit, no state deletion. A stale cached quota of 2/4 (real
value 4/4) nearly authorised a POST into an exhausted quota, and a 403 there is permanent.
2. NEVER RESTART BLIND. watchdog.py restarted a dead driver with its ORIGINAL argv and ran the
wrong pool for 25 minutes while the correct driver sat blocked on the lock. A restart must
re-derive its own arguments, which is why restart_driver calls a script rather than

clear_lock.why: resim.lock exists with no live holder; the next round would wait 30min for nothing

restart_driver.why: driver gone or journal stale; re-derives pool and hours instead of replaying argv

kill_extra_drivers.why: two drivers contend for one sim lock; the older one is the stale resurrection

ensure_harvester.why: screen the un-measured backlog from PnL curves. NOT harvest_corr.py: the platform never queues correlation work for old alphas (/check returns in 1s still showing SELF_CORRELATION PENDING), so that tool ran 36 minutes, added one record and 429'd the account. PnL curves DO compute on demand and give sharpe, the 2-year ladder and self-correlation -- three of the four hard gates.

refresh_quota.why: quota reading too old to act on

escalate.why: needs judgement — hand to the expensive supervisor with the snapshot attached

_escalate_notes.QUOTA_OPEN: Spending a submit slot needs the family matrix and the cell plan. Four slots inside one signal family unlock nothing, and a submit is irreversible.
_escalate_notes.NO_CLEAN_DESPITE_PASSERS: This has had three different root causes already (measure budget too short, park queue stranded, circuit breaker skipping the trigger request). It is not a runbook case.
